summary: Jonathan Christopher Cleary (1947–2023) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed doctoral work at Harvard University (~1976–1982) under Masatoshi Nagatomi and served as an instructor at Wesleyan University.

Jonathan Duquette is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who earned his PhD from the Université de Montréal (2005–2011). He held fellowships at Oxford (2015–2019) and Birmingham (2020–2021), and was an affiliated lecturer at Cambridge in 2019.

Jonathan Edelmann works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He completed his DPhil at the University of Oxford in 2009 and was appointed assistant professor at the University of Florida in 2015.

Jonathan Geen is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed his doctorate at McMaster University in 2001 under Phyllis Granoff. He has held teaching posts at McMaster University, Butler University, and the University of Rochester.

Jonathan Glover (born 1941) is a philosopher educated at Tonbridge School and Corpus Christi College, Oxford (~1960–1963). He served as fellow and tutor at New College (~1967–1998) and held posts at King's College London (~1998–2013) and Oxford (~2013).

Jonathan Lear (1948–2025) was a philosopher who studied at Yale, Cambridge, Rockefeller, and the Western New England Institute. He taught at Yale (1978–1996), Cambridge and Clare College (~1979–1985), and the University of Chicago (2014–2022).

Jonathan Mark Kenoyer (born 1952) specializes in archaeology and Indology. Educated at Woodstock School and UC Berkeley (~1970–1983) under George F. Dales, he became a professor of anthropology at the University of Wisconsin-Madison around 1985.

Jonathan Scott (1754–1829) was an Indology and Iranian/Central Asian scholar who co-founded The Asiatic Society. He served as professor of Oriental languages at the Royal Military College, Sandhurst (1802) and the East India Company College (~1802–1805).

Jonathan Z. Smith (1938–2017) was a religious studies scholar who studied at Haverford and Yale. He taught at Dartmouth (~1965–1966) and UC Santa Barbara (~1966–1969) before serving as Dean of the College at Chicago (1977–1982).

Jong-Nam Choi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Shitennoji University and the University of Hamburg (PhD 1998) under Lambert Schmithausen, also studying under S. A. Srinivasan, Albrecht Wezler, and David Seyfort Ruegg.

Jongcheol Lee (born 1954) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Seoul National University and the University of Tokyo (PhD 1994, under Yasunori Ejima), held a research post at Mysore (1992), and joined AKS (attested 2001).

Jongmyung Kim is a scholar of Korean Buddhism, history, and religious studies. Educated at Yonsei, Seoul National, and UCLA (MA 1994 under Robert E. Buswell Jr.), he became an associate professor at the Academy of Korean Studies (attested 2012–2019).

Joryu Chiba (1921–2008) was a Japanese historian and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1939–1950). He held faculty posts at Ryukoku from 1950, becoming honorary professor (1970–1989), and directed multiple Buddhist research institutes.

Jos Gommans (born 1963) is a historian and Indologist educated at Radboud University and Leiden University (PhD under Jan C. Heesterman and André Wink). He was an NWO fellow (1989–1993) and became a professor at Leiden in 2011.

Jos. Schrijnen (1869–1938) was a linguist who earned his PhD from KU Leuven (1891) and studied in Paris. He served as professor at Utrecht University (1912–1923) and was professor and rector at Radboud University Nijmegen (1923–1938).

Josef Baudiš (1883–1933) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Charles University (under Josef Zubatý) and Heidelberg University. He served as Privatdozent at Charles University (~1910–1914) and became a professor at Comenius University in 1924.

Josef Friedrich Kohl (1908–1998) was an Indologist who studied at the German University in Prague and the University of Bonn (PhD ~1937 under Willibald Kirfel). He served as Privatdozent at Bonn and Prague, and later professor at Würzburg (1957).

Josef Horovitz (1874–1931) studied at Marburg and Humboldt University of Berlin (PhD under Eduard Sachau). He taught at Berlin (1902), served as Professor of Arabic at Aligarh (1907–1914), and became a professor at Frankfurt in 1915.
Josef Jungmann (1773–1847) was a linguist who studied at Charles University in 1795 and later served there in an academic post from approximately 1815 to 1845.

Josef Kohler (1849–1919) was a scholar of law, Indology, and history. He studied at Heidelberg and Freiburg (doctorate ~1873) and served as a professor at the University of Würzburg (1878) and Humboldt University of Berlin (from 1888).
